source.title: PROBLEMS AND CONJECTURES AROUND SHIFT RADIX SYSTEMS

accepted.question_text: For each dimension d ≥ 2, give a complete description of the parameter sets D_d and D_d^(0) associated with shift radix systems. Here, for r = (r_0, ..., r_{d-1}) ∈ R^d, the shift radix system τ_r: Z^d → Z^d is defined by τ_r(z_0, ..., z_{d-1}) = (z_1, ..., z_{d-1}, -⌊r_0 z_0 + ··· + r_{d-1} z_{d-1}⌋)^t. The set D_d consists of those r for which every orbit of τ_r on Z^d is ultimately periodic, and D_d^(0) consists of those r for which τ_r has the finiteness property, meaning that for every z ∈ Z^d there exists k ∈ N such that τ_r^k(z) = 0.

evidence.quote: Problem 2.2. Give a complete description of Dd and D (0) d for each d ≥ 2.

accepted.question_text: Determine the computational complexity of deciding membership in D_d^(0) for rational parameters. More precisely, for a fixed dimension d and a rational vector r ∈ Q^d, prove that the property r ∈ D_d^(0) cannot be verified in polynomial time, and decide whether this decision problem lies outside the complexity class NP.

evidence.quote: Problem 2.3. Prove that r ∈ D(0) d ∩ Qd cannot be verified in polynomial time. Is it true that this problem does not belong to the NP complexity class?

accepted.question_text: Characterize all parameter vectors r for which the digit expansions in the number systems associated with the shift radix system τ_r form a language that is a sofic shift.

evidence.quote: Problem 2.4. Characterize all parameters r for which the digits of the underlying number systems gives a language of a sofic shift (see [18] for the definition).

accepted.question_text: Is every parameter vector r for which the shift radix system τ_r has the finiteness property contained in the Schur-Cohn region E_d? Equivalently, does the inclusion D_d^(0) ⊂ E_d always hold, where E_d is the set of all r ∈ R^d for which the companion polynomial χ_r(X) = X^d + r_{d-1}X^{d-1} + ··· + r_1X + r_0 is contractive?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2.5. We have D (0) d ⊂ Ed.

accepted.question_text: Determine the geometric and topological structure of D_d^(0), the set of parameters r for which the shift radix system τ_r has the finiteness property. In particular, what is the measure of D_d^(0), what can be said about its topology, and what is the Hausdorff dimension of its boundary?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.6. What is the measure of D (0) d ? What can we say about the topology of D (0) d ? What is the Hausdorff dimension of the boundary of D (0) d ?

accepted.question_text: Is the fundamental group of D_3^(0) non-trivial? More specifically, does the three-dimensional finiteness region D_3^(0) contain a topological handle?
accepted.context_brief: Topology of the three-dimensional finiteness region

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2.7. The fundamental group of D (0) 3 is non-trivial, i.e., it has a handle.

accepted.question_text: Given a rational parameter vector r ∈ E_d ∩ Q^d, decide whether membership in D_d is algorithmically decidable. Here D_d is the set of parameters for which every orbit of the shift radix system τ_r on Z^d is ultimately periodic.

evidence.quote: Problem 2.8. Given r ∈ Ed ∩ Qd , is r ∈ Dd algorithmically decidable?

accepted.question_text: Let λ ∈ R satisfy -2 < λ < 2, let a_0, a_1 ∈ Z, and define a recurrence by a_{n+1} := -a_{n-1} - ⌊λ a_n⌋ for n ≥ 1. Is the sequence a_0, a_1, a_2, ... always periodic?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2.9. Let λ ∈ R be such that −2 < λ < 2. Further, let a0, a1 ∈ Z and define an+1 := −an−1 − bλanc (n ≥ 1). Then the sequence a0, a1, a2, . . . is periodic.

accepted.question_text: For the recurrence a_{n+1} := -a_{n-1} - ⌊λ a_n⌋, do there exist infinitely many non-symmetric periodic orbits for every real parameter λ?

evidence.quote: A weaker conjecture is that for any λ there exist infinitely many non-symmetric periodic orbits.

accepted.question_text: Let E_d^(C) = {r ∈ ∂E_d : R_r has a non-real eigenvalue of modulus 1}. For which parameters r ∈ E_d^(C) is every orbit of the shift radix system τ_r ultimately periodic? In particular, for which such r is the orbit of the vector (1, 0, ..., 0)^t ultimately periodic?
accepted.context_brief: Ultimate periodicity on the boundary hypersurface

evidence.quote: Problem 2.10. For which r ∈ E (C) d is each orbit of τr ultimately periodic, in particular the orbit of (1, 0, . . . , 0)t ?

accepted.question_text: Let r ∈ E_d^(C) be such that the companion polynomial χ_r is irreducible, and let s be the number of pairs of complex conjugate roots (α, ᾱ) of χ_r with |α| = 1. Is it true that every orbit of (1, 0, ..., 0)^t under τ_r is periodic when s ∈ {1, 2}, while for s ≥ 3 there exist parameters r for which the orbit of (1, 0, ..., 0)^t is aperiodic?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2.11. Let r ∈ E (C) d be such that χr is irreducible. Let s be the number of pairs of complex conjugate roots (α, α¯) of χr with |α| = 1. Then every orbit of (1, 0, . . . , 0)t under τr is periodic if s ∈ {1, 2}, and there exist r such that the orbit of (1, 0, . . . , 0)t is aperiodic if s ≥ 3 (see also [12], [13]).

accepted.question_text: For a parameter r ∈ E_d and each z ∈ Z^d with r_0 ≠ 0, define the SRS tile by T_r(z) = Lim_{n→∞} R_r^n τ_r^{-n}({z}), where the limit is taken in the Hausdorff metric. Is the collection of tiles {T_r(z) : z ∈ Z^d} always a tiling of R^d, meaning a collection of compact sets that covers R^d with zero-measure overlaps?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2.13. Let r ∈ Ed. Then {Tr(z) : z ∈ Z d} is a tiling of R d .

accepted.question_text: Let r ∈ E_d, let z ∈ Z^d, and let T_r(z) be the associated SRS tile. Give criteria that characterize when T_r(z) is equal to the closure of its interior.
accepted.context_brief: Interior-closure criterion for an SRS tile

evidence.quote: Problem 2.14. Let r ∈ Ed and z ∈ Z d . Give criteria for Tr(z) being the closure of its interior.

accepted.question_text: For dimensions d ≥ 2, describe the set of parameters r ∈ E_d for which the central SRS tile T_r(0) is connected; equivalently, describe the Mandelbrot-type sets {r ∈ E_d : T_r(0) is connected}.
accepted.context_brief: Connectivity locus of central SRS tiles

evidence.quote: Problem 2.15. Describe the Mandelbrot sets {r ∈ Ed : Tr(0) is connected} for d ≥ 2.
